messages:
maria: urgent — high-sev ticket from customer on Dedicated (private VPC). After their SSO IdP rotated keys, a subset of users get 401 from our API. They claim the original request includes Authorization: Bearer <token> at their L7 proxy, but when it hits our private gateway the header is missing. Repro steps they provided below.

maria: repro steps (from customer):
```bash
curl -i -H "Host: api.customer.internal" -H "Authorization: Bearer ey..." \n  https://<customer-lb>/v1/generate
```
They see 200 at their LB but our gw logs show: `missing auth header` and request gets 401 from our auth middleware.

maria: observed behavior:
- LB (ALB) access logs contain the Authorization header.
- tcpdump on gateway frontend shows the TCP packets, but when we inspect the HTTP headers in our edge handler they're absent.
- this started after the customer's IdP rotation but only for some routes.

tom: pinging eng-infra/ingress folks. quick q: is the customer terminating TLS at an external proxy then re-issuing a request to our GW? if so that proxy could be intentionally dropping Authorization for forwarded requests.

maria: yes, they terminate TLS on an nginx-based L7 proxy inside their VPC and then proxy_pass to our dedicated endpoint over mTLS. they've sent snippets of config.

rui: can you paste the nginx config snippet? common culprits: `proxy_set_header Authorization $http_authorization;` missing or `proxy_pass_request_headers off`. Also `underscores_in_headers` shows up sometimes.

maria: here's the snippet they shared (sanitized):
```nginx
server {
  listen 443 ssl;
  location / {
    proxy_pass https://our-dedicated-endpoint:443;
    proxy_set_header Host $host;
    proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
    # no explicit proxy_set_header Authorization here
  }
}
```

sam: that lines up. nginx will not forward the Authorization header unless `proxy_set_header Authorization $http_authorization;` is explicit when doing `proxy_pass` to HTTPS upstreams in some versions. also double-check `proxy_hide_header` or `proxy_pass_request_headers`.

neha: also confirm they're not normalizing header case or using `Authorization` vs `authorization` variants — our gateway expects `Authorization`. Envoy/Istio normalize but custom proxies can mangle. add an internal debug route that echoes headers so we can see exact names.

maria: customer tried curl to that debug route and it returned headers with `authorization` present at their lb-level echo, but our edge route echo shows none.

tom: if they're using Istio or Envoy in front of our endpoint (e.g., sidecar or ingress) look for `remove_user_headers` or `strip_authorization_header` flags in filter chains. Example envoy config to preserve:
```yaml
http_filters:
- name: envoy.filters.http.lua
  typed_config:
    '@type': type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.http.lua.v3.Lua
    inline_code: |
      function envoy_on_request(request_handle)
        -- don't strip authorization
      end
```
# or ensure route: `allow_headers: "authorization"`

rui: specifically for Istio 1.12+ check `meshConfig.defaultConfig.exitNodePull` (no that's unrelated) — sorry. The real thing is header whitelist in `VirtualService`/`Gateway` for some older ingress controllers. For Envoy: `route: request_headers_to_add` and `preserve_host`. For NGINX: add `proxy_set_header Authorization $http_authorization;`.

sam: security note — if the customer re-signs tokens or injects headers we need to ensure they don't accidentally expose creds. but forwarding original Authorization is fine over mTLS path. verify mTLS is in place.

neha: action plan I propose:
1) add a temporary debug endpoint on the dedicated gateway that returns `X-RW-RECV-AUTH: <present|missing>` and dumps raw headers (only enabled for 24h + restricted by allowlist).
2) ask customer to hit debug endpoint and paste results.
3) if header missing, ask them to add `proxy_set_header Authorization $http_authorization;` in nginx and retest.
4) if header present to LB but still missing to us, capture sidecar/istio config and any envoy filters that manipulate headers.

maria: customer agreed to step 1 & 3. trying now.

deploy-bot: patch queued: `dedicated-gw: add-debug-route-1793456789` — rollout to canary in 2 mins :rocket:

maria: canary live. customer hit it and returned: `X-RW-RECV-AUTH: missing` and headers dump shows Authorization absent. their LB echo still shows `Authorization: Bearer ey...` so the drop is between their LB and our gateway (likely their proxy config).

tom: confirm they have `proxy_set_header Authorization $http_authorization;` added and they restarted nginx.

maria: they added the line and restarted, re-tested: debug route now returns `X-RW-RECV-AUTH: present` and our service responded 200 for previously failing users. customer reports resolution. :tada:

sam: great. followups: ask customer to keep the explicit header line in nginx config and add it to their deploy checklist. we should add a KB article about common proxy header drops for Dedicated/Private setups (nginx, ALB, Istio/Envoy snippets).

neha: I'll file a quick internal playbook and assign to eng-docs to publish KB. action items: neha -> create KB; tom -> add small note in onboarding docs for Dedicated about verifying header passthrough; maria -> confirm ticket closure with customer and ensure we get confirmation in 24h.

maria: will close after 24h and paste confirmation here. thanks all!
